title: 我构建 AI DevList 是因为寻找 AI 内容已不再是问题
author: Younes Ben Tlili
content:
There is no shortage of AI content.

Actually, we probably have the opposite problem.

Every day there is:

  • a new agent framework,
  • a new MCP server,
  • another RAG approach,
  • another benchmark,
  • another model release,
  • another “production-ready” architecture,
  • another GitHub repository trendi ng for 48 hours.

As an engineer, I don't struggle to find AI content anymore.

I struggle to decide:

What is actually worth my time?

That's why I built AI DevList.

👉 https://aidevlist.io/

Not another AI news newsletter

I don't want AI DevList to become a summary of everything that happened in AI during the week.

There are already excellent newsletters doing that.

The focus is much narrower:

resources that are useful for people actually building AI systems.

The main topics are:

  • Agentic AI
  • LLM Engineering
  • MCP
  • RAG
  • Evals
  • Tools & Frameworks
  • Research
  • Open Source
  • Production AI

The goal is not to publish 50 links.

If an issue contains 10–15 genuinely useful resources, that's enough.

Curation alone isn't enough

When I first announced the project, someone gave me a very good piece of feedback:

Curating content is useful, but the real value comes from adding context.

I agree.

So every resource selected for AI DevList now has two parts.

1. What is it?

A short, neutral description of the resource.

No marketing rewrite.

No exaggerated claims.

2. Why we picked it

This is the important part.

For example:

Why we picked it
Stateless MCP isn't just a protocol detail. It changes how remote MCP servers can be deployed and scaled, removing part of the session-management complexity that infrastructure teams previously had to handle.

Or:

Why we picked it
Adding a SKILL.md file doesn't guarantee that an agent will reliably discover or follow it. This benchmark is interesting because it evaluates the complete model + harness + skill combination rather than treating skills as static prompt files.

That's much closer to what I personally want when someone recommends a technical article to me.

Don't only tell me what it says.

Tell me why I should care as an engineer.

My current curation workflow

The workflow is deliberately simple.

Discover resources
↓
Filter obvious noise
↓
Read / inspect the source
↓
Check technical relevance
↓
Categorize
↓
Write a short description
↓
Add "Why we picked it"
↓
Human review
↓
Publish

AI helps with discovery and preparation.

It does not decide what gets published.

That's an important distinction for me.

I don't want to build an automatically generated newsletter that summarizes whatever happens to rank highly that week.

The final selection remains editorial.

What makes a resource worth selecting?

I'm currently using a few simple questions.

Is it technically credible?

Primary sources, engineering blogs, research papers and serious open-source work get priority.

Does it solve a real engineering problem?

Observability, reliability, security, evaluations, context management, orchestration, infrastructure, cost...

Not just demos.

Can someone apply something from it?

Even research becomes much more interesting when it changes how we think about architecture or implementation.

Is it saying something new?

Ten articles repeating the same product announcement don't deserve ten slots.

Is it worth 10 minutes of someone's time?

This may actually be the most important criterion.

Attention is expensive.

The first issue

I'm currently preparing AI DevList #001, which will be published on August 23.

Some of the topics I'm reviewing include:

  1. emerging behavior in multi-agent systems,
  2. MCP architecture and security,
  3. testing agent skills,
  4. malicious skill files,
  5. agent observability,
  6. authorization for autonomous workflows,
  7. production evaluation patterns.

I'm intentionally keeping the first issue relatively small.

I'd rather publish 12 strong resources than 40 average ones.

This is also an experiment

AI DevList is a small project.

The application itself is intentionally boring:

  • Next.js
  • PostgreSQL
  • Docker
  • GitLab CI/CD

The interesting problem isn't the software.

It's whether consistent technical curation can become useful enough that engineers return every week.

Over the next few months, I want to learn:

  • Which topics engineers actually click on?
  • Do people prefer research or practical engineering articles?
  • Are MCP resources still disproportionately interesting?
  • How much context is enough before curation becomes commentary?
  • Can a small, focused technical publication build a meaningful engineering audience?

I have added click analytics from the beginning so I can answer some of those questions with data instead of intuition.

If you're building AI systems

You can subscribe here:

👉 https://aidevlist.io/

The first issue comes out on August 23.

And if you publish a technical article, paper, open-source project or tool that you think AI engineers should see, there is also a submission page:

👉 https://aidevlist.io/submit

I'm especially interested in feedback from engineers:

What would make a curated AI engineering weekly genuinely useful enough for you to read every week?
aiSummary: 一位 AI 工程师分享了 AI DevList 的理念和工作流程。这是一份精心策划的通讯，专注于为构建 AI 系统的人提供实用资源，强调基于上下文的精选而非数量。
oneSentenceSummary: 一位 AI 工程师分享了 AI DevList 的理念和工作流程。这是一份精心策划的通讯，专注于为构建 AI 系统的人提供实用资源，强调基于上下文的精选而非数量。
summary: 作者探讨了 AI 内容过载的悖论：材料太多而非太少，工程师难以辨别真正值得投入时间的内容。为此，他们构建了 AI DevList，一份聚焦于 Agentic AI、LLM 工程、MCP、RAG、Evals 和生产 AI 的通讯。与摘要式通讯不同，每个精选资源都包含中性描述和'为何选择它'部分，解释工程相关性。策展工作流程刻意保持简单且以人为驱动，AI 仅协助发现和准备。筛选标准优先考虑技术可信度、实际工程问题解决能力、适用性和新颖性。首期于 8 月 23 日推出，主题包括多智能体涌现行为、MCP 安全、智能体可观测性和生产评估模式。该项目也被定位为一次实验，测试持续的技术策展能否随时间建立忠诚的工程受众。

mainPoints.point: AI 的真正问题在于内容过载，而非稀缺。
mainPoints.explanation: 每日输出的新框架、基准测试和代码库，使工程师更难识别值得关注的內容，将挑战从发现转向筛选。

mainPoints.point: 策展的价值在于与上下文结合，而非仅仅提供链接。
mainPoints.explanation: 每个资源都包含'为何选择它'部分，解释工程相关性，例如无状态 MCP 如何改变部署复杂度，或基准测试为何评估完整的模型-工具链-技能组合。

mainPoints.point: 策展工作流程刻意保持简单且以人为驱动。
mainPoints.explanation: AI 协助发现与准备，但最终选择仍由编辑决定。流程从发现经过筛选、检查、分类、描述，再到人工审核后才发布。

mainPoints.point: 筛选标准优先考虑技术可信度和工程实用性，而非仅新颖性。
mainPoints.explanation: 资源必须解决真实的工程问题（可观测性、可靠性、安全、评估），具备实践者可直接应用性，并有所创新。作者将注意力视为昂贵资源，询问每个资源是否值得 10 分钟阅读时间。

mainPoints.point: 该项目也是一次建立忠诚工程受众的实验。
mainPoints.explanation: 作者计划追踪点击分析，了解哪些主题引发共鸣，工程师是否偏好研究或实用文章，以及小型聚焦通讯能否在数月内维持参与度。

keyQuotes: 作为工程师，我不再为找不到 AI 内容而困扰。我困扰的是：什么真正值得我花时间？
策展内容有用，但真正的价值在于添加上下文。
无状态 MCP 不只是协议细节。它改变了远程 MCP 服务器的部署和扩展方式，消除了基础设施团队之前必须处理的会话管理复杂度的一部分。
我宁愿发布 12 个高质量资源，而非 40 个平庸的。
